title: Let’s Take a Look at GW’s Caverns of the Dead, Dungeon Lairs and Dungeon Rooms
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7EgU3ReHrIc

Daniel (@dungeondive) gathers three old Games Workshop supplements into one video "for archival reasons." The star is Caverns of the Dead, a Dungeon Planner set from the days when GW made system-neutral material for RuneQuest, Dungeons & Dragons and others. He bought it for the Gary Chalk cover (the line work, the expressive faces, the skeletons) and notes Chalk designed the set as well. The box is held together with tape. Inside are a GM screen with encounter and activity tables, a fold-out card map of the royal tombs at 25mm scale, a regional map of Eastern Coasts that suggests the series was meant to join into a campaign setting, and a room-by-room booklet with the previous owner's notes in it. He has never seen another set for sale.

Dungeon Lairs and Dungeon Rooms follow. The box promises "stout cardboard," which turns out to be about two sheets of paper thick, and the previous owner of his eBay copies had laminated them. He wishes the tiles had grids and shows his experiments printing grids on transparency.

One spiral-staircase tile always takes him back to Boletaria in Demon's Souls. He muses that someone should make a Dark Souls board game, then remembers someone did.

----

Gary Chalk's cover sold Daniel this box on its own. What cover art has made you buy a game or supplement sight unseen?
